title: Vampire Castle
text: “I see. Well, there’s that saying about first spear and all, so shall we have Motoyasu-san go in? It seems like the levels inside the labyrinth get reflected separately.”
“I shall show you how it’s done!”
“Motoyasu-sama! Fight, fight!”
Since Yuki-chan was cheering me on, I simply had to show off my best side.
“Then I’m off, indeed!”
I dashed out of the circle, grabbed the lantern, and ran straight through the door, indeed!
“Just to confirm… yep, there’s still a transparent wall in front of the door. It looks like only Motoyasu-san holding the lantern can pass through.”
“Character Change is… oh, looks like it can be done from this side too.”

A voice spoke from the lantern, and with a *bwoosh*, my vision suddenly switched. Before I knew it, I was standing in a circle marked with the spear crest. In the center of the room, within the gate’s projected image, Father stood, waving his hand.
“I see, so entering the circle lets you switch, and there’s a Level displayed in the top left of the screen. Is this tracked individually?”
“Seems like it needs verification, but… oh, the status is displayed on the stone tablet. The Level appears to be shared, or rather, it’s the lantern’s Level.”
“It’s Father, indeed!”
I waved back at Father. Could he even see me, I wonder?
“Alright, Motoyasu-kun, switching you back now.”
With another *bwoosh*, my vision switched back, and I returned to my previous location.
“So the camera angle is fixed on that room, it seems.”
“Must be nice just watching.”
“Anyway, Motoyasu-san, please proceed forward as you are.”
“I find Itsuki’s orders questionable, but understood, indeed!”

*Thud-thud-thud!* I advanced through the castle. Then, in the corridor, a monster appeared—a Purple Soul Whip, some sort of ghost-type creature. I tried to unleash Brionac, but the skill wouldn’t activate.
“Air Strike Javelin, indeed!”

With a *shwoosh*, the Purple Soul Whip was blown away with ease, and experience points came pouring in. Quite a decent amount, too. It might’ve been classified as trash mob fodder, but the payout wasn’t bad at all, was it?
“I could see the experience display. That’s… quite a lot, isn’t it?”
“Yeah. Separate from the lantern’s Level, it looks like Motoyasu himself is also gaining experience—how does that work?”
“It’s coming in, indeed.”
“According to the stone tablet’s explanation, monsters respawn when you cross between zones…”

Time to test that by going in and out of a room! I stepped from the corridor into a room and immediately back out, and sure enough, the Purple Soul Whip was there again. I loosed an Air Strike Javelin at once, and the lantern’s Level hit 2.
“That’s a fast respawn.”
“Conversely, the downside is having to fight again every time you pass through, even after defeating one.”
“Couldn’t you just ignore it and push through? Well, farming them along the way for extra experience isn’t a bad idea either.”
“Hmm…”
“Seems good for grinding, though. Anyway, please just keep pushing forward, Motoyasu-san.”
“No need for Itsuki to tell me twice, indeed!”
And so, with my swift feet, I forged ahead at a brisk pace!
“Huh, maybe it’s because Motoyasu-kun is an Usaunny, but he’s pretty fast running solo. Ren as an Inult might be able to match that speed?”
“Who knows.”
“Seems like there might be racial traits at play here too, on top of whatever elements carried over from that earlier dungeon.”
While I listened to Father and the others chatting away, I cut down every monster that appeared, one after another.
“Take that! Indeed!”
All sorts of monsters showed up here. Apparently they were illusions, but they varied wildly.
“The drops are like medicinal herbs and… there should be cheap knives and swords too, but it seems those aren’t actually obtainable.”
“Wait a moment. It looks like rare items do drop.”
“So weapon materials for each weapon type and rare items do appear…”
“Nano, is this like the heroes’ treasure vault, like in the Prado Desert?”
Rival tilted her head slightly as she asked Father and the others.

“It’s said to be a training ground for the heroes, so the items hidden there might be things that get unlocked and obtained here just by defeating the monster illusions… probably generating the weapons for us.”
“I see, nano. If this place hadn’t been hidden, the heroes probably wouldn’t have had anything to fear from the Waves, nano.”
“…That’s plausible. Maybe this is the real hidden dungeon they wanted to keep secret precisely because Motoyasu never knew about it.”
“I wonder about the pointlessly elaborate design choices here.”
“Still, the experience Motoyasu’s racking up by clearing things so effortlessly is pretty substantial. Imagine how much he’ll get once he goes deeper and starts taking down stronger monsters.”

While Father and the others analyzed away like that, the lantern’s Level climbed all the way to 20. Absurdly, effortlessly easy. And since it was a dungeon, there were naturally plenty of branching paths. I pressed onward through them more or less at random.
“Just occurred to me—if there’s a racial gimmick here too, wouldn’t we need to have Ren, who can sniff out hidden items, deployed by default?”
“Father. Don’t underestimate my nose, indeed. I’ll sniff things out better than Ren’s nose ever could.”
“Whatever are they competing over, I wonder.”
“Let’s just leave it to Motoyasu. Looking at the map, I think it’s pretty easy to guess where the hidden rooms are.”
Seemed like Ren didn’t want to be deployed, so he handed exploration duties over to me.

“Well… given this dungeon comes with a full map and, like, the whole ‘explore inside a castle’ gimmick, it feels like what people commonly call a Metr●idvania. Probably because of the map on this side.”
Father muttered that.
“I’ve played similar games too. It’s definitely got that exploration-focused 2D game feel.”
“Right. On Motoyasu-kun’s side it’s probably a proper dungeon, but on our screen it really looks like a 2D action game.”
“What genre exactly is this, anyway?”

“Well… the famous one is basically a game where you storm a vampire’s castle and take him down. You go wherever you can, beat the boss of the area, and the items or abilities you get afterward keep opening up more places to explore.”

Vampires, was it? Come to think of it, over in Siltvelt there was apparently a race that kept trying to become vampires generation after generation, all because the Shield Hero had wished for it once. I recalled that years later, when Father visited Siltvelt, he’d issued a decree telling them they didn’t need to be so devoted to polishing up their bloodline anymore.
“Hoh… I thought I’d played plenty of games myself, but I guess there was one like this too. Feels vaguely familiar, though I never knew the details.”

“It’s just that Naofumi-san has played an absurd amount of games. Honestly, it’d be more surprising if this world didn’t have something similar. Vampires… oh, come to think of it, doesn’t the name of the activation site sound like it’s related? Wasn’t there one called Dracia?”

“Right. Dracula, Carmilla, Nosferatu, Vlad—they’re all corrupted names for settlement sites… Don’t tell me some past hero named this place ironically while conquering this very castle? Itsuki! What do you think?”
“I have no idea! Don’t try to build some weird theory around my naming sense!”

Thanks to Father’s speculation, a theory emerged about the origin of the activation site’s name. I wonder what the truth actually was. In any case, it seemed the objective here was to clear the vampire’s castle. Which meant the ultimate goal was to become the master of this castle, indeed.
“Shall I clear this place and become Vampire Motoyasu, then?”
Me, decked out in a vampire’s cape! Fuhahahaha! Something like that, indeed.
“I feel like it’d suit your original form, but right now you’re an Usaunny, you know.”
“Truly fancy.”
“Father, between vampire me and Usaunny vampire me, which do you prefer?”
“You’re seriously asking me to choose between those two!?”

Father’s voice came out sounding rather troubled. Meanwhile, I found myself imagining what Filo-tan would look like as a vampire. Oh? Come to think of it, after peace had come, Filo-tan dressed up in costume for the village’s Halloween celebration once, didn’t she?
